ruling.reasoning:
The driver cancelled this trip (✗ NS-0 trace, [F4]), so the only chargeable path is the no-show fee, and the $5.00 on record [F8] stands only if every NS-1 condition holds [NS-1][NS-0]. The trace settles arrival (driver tapped "I'm Here" at 22:39:00, 40 m from the pickup) [F7] and the free wait (360 s continuously at the pickup counted from arrival, threshold 300 s) [F7], so NS-1(i) and NS-1(ii) are met.

The decisive condition is NS-1(iii): before cancelling the driver must have sent at least one in-app message AND made at least one in-app call [NS-1]. The timeline records 2 in-app messages (first 22:39:30) but 0 in-app calls [F5], and the driver's own statement — written after the trip, in his own words — confirms "I messaged the rider in the app; I did not call" [F13]. The message limb is therefore met by F10/F11 but the call limb is not, and both briefs concede this point. Continuous presence is also satisfied: the driver was stationary 41 m away for 6 min 5 s [F3], within 200 m from 22:38:40 for 6 min 20 s cumulative [F2].

Any NS-1 condition failing voids the fee [NS-2]. The amount is the fixed cancellation fee on record, $5.00 [F8][NS-1]; no surge applied (1.0×) [F9], so no FARE-0 build-up or surge differential arises and no NS-8 goodwill credit is available (the driver did arrive [F7] and did message [F5]). Nothing in the record makes this a driver-cancellation-for-another-reason case: the app reason was rider_no_show and he remained at the pickup [F4][F3], so NS-3 does not apply.

Safety: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement [F10][F11][F13]; they are a routine waiting-and-cancelling exchange with no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation [SAFE-1]. Evidence: the record contains the GPS positions, timestamped messages and the app reason, so every element this ruling needs is settled [TH-4]; the fee is $5.00, a fixed no-show amount decided by the system [TH-2].

The fee cannot be upheld merely because the amount and multiplier are correct: NS-1 is conjunctive and the call limb failed (0 calls [F5]; driver admits no call [F13]), which voids the fee under NS-2 regardless of the amount [NS-1][NS-2].
Asked not to judge the rider's no-show narrative: profile/history facts never decide the case [F17][NS-9], and no credibility point changes the conjunctive NS-1(iii) failure [F5][F13].
The driver's long record and 0 upheld disputes [F18] cannot cure a failed NS-1 condition; NS-1 is a checklist, not a credibility contest, and the trace settles the checklist [NS-1].
